question: Megasthenes, a Greek historian and diplomat came to India as an ambassador of Seleucus I Nicator. In which of the following Mauryan emperor’s court did he come?
solution:
The correct answer is**__ Chandragupta Maurya__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Megasthenes was a great historian, author, and diplomat.
 
• His book, **Indica** gives a major glimpse into ancient **Mauryan India**.
 
• He was an ambassador to Mauryan Emperor** Chandragupta**, sent by the Hellenistic King** Seleucus I**.
 
• He described the physiography of India along with the magnificence of the Mauryan Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya**

 
 
• **​**He founded Mauryan Empire by the culmination of three successive dynasties - **The Haryanka dynasty, the Sisunaga dynasty, and the Nanda dynasty** in the 4th century BC.
 
• He took the glory of the Mauryan Empire to its peak by fighting victorious battles and administrating in a progressive manner.
 
• He bought a vast region under his control including **Bihar, Orissa, and Bengal**, along with the North and Northwestern part of the subcontinent.
 
• He kept all the powers centralized for efficient administration.
 
• Earlier he practiced **Hinduism** and then embraced **Jainism**.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka**
 
 
• He reigned from 268-232 BCE and kept on the expansion of the empire.
 
• He invaded **Kalinga **in **261 BC** and succeeded in occupying it.
 
• After his conquest of Kalinga, he abandoned an armed victory for '**Victory by Dhamma'**.
 
• He embraced **Buddhism **after the Kalinga War and worked for its propagation through the **Edicts of Buddhism **across South Asia and the European Subcontinent.
 
• **Brihardrath** was the **last ruler** of the Mauryan Empire, he was killed by his Brahman commander-in-chief,** Pushyamitra**, who then founded the **Shunga dynasty**.
